How did you lose faith in Christianity?

Took me damn long while to lose my faith - it was definitely an emotional crutch to help me through a lot of psychological issues I had when I was younger.

In the end though? Over about 10 years, read lots of Christian apologetics as well as atheist rebuttals, viewpoints and reasoning. My faith slowly leaked out of me, like air out of a tire, until one day, that tire -- belief -- was flat. I just didn't believe anymore.

There were no "silver bullet" arguments for me; just a slow, persistent and, dare I say, inevitable loss of faith.

Are you out to your family/friends?

I'm out to a couple of close friends. My family? Only my big sis who hasn't believed since she was about 6 years old (and she's keeping it a secret). The rest? Nope. Coz they couldn't handle the fallout from it if I did. It would drop a psychological nuclear bomb on them, despite how much they love me.

What are you now?

Hrm I can't really pinpoint how I lost my faith. I do remember it was sometime in middle school. I remember when I found out that a good friend of mine was atheist and I just couldn't comprehend how he could be. I was reading the bible for the first time and I noticed the inaccuracies and it bothered me. I then spent a solid six months researching alternative religions wicca, buddhism, hinduism, etc. Until I came to the conclusion that I was a freelance theist. I subscribed to a personal god but didn't claim to know anything beyond that. I think then sometime around 8th grade it finally hit me that it was all bullshit and the bubble finally popped when I read Scumbag: Musings of a subhuman. A book by the amazing atheist.

Are you out? Yes I am out to my family and friends in fact most of my friends are atheist I went to an art high school so lot's of intelligent people who are atheist. I was raised with little to no organized religion, no regular church going just a sense that there was a god, no matter how ill defined, Then in 7th grade I was transferred into a Lutheran School, catechism recitals "from memory" in the mornings and full on godly mindfiul instruction all day straight through graduation of 8th grade. Prayers at lunch, prayers at basketball games, it was all "normal".

I suppose it never really took but in the summer break of my freshman year of HS (and back in public school), on a bus, I came across a chick tract that told me that all I had to do was accept jesus, even in the last millisecond before i died and was be guaranteed to be saved and transported to heaven instead of hell, no matter what else I did.

The absurdity of my actions and actual beliefs having nothing whatsoever to do with my destination made me think that those that believed in that mechanism, and that god were complete fools.

I then embarked on an exploration of all of the major religions that had representation available available in the Chicago area and every single one was at least as absurd as christianity.

Many had admirable messages and frankly the minimization of suffering that buddhism represents is very attractive to me but in the end I simply cannot believe that any god worth my worship would allow so much suffering among so many innocents and then forgive me a lifetime of offenses for a millisecond's supposed belief.

So, I guess you could say that a chick track made me an atheist. I hope Mr Chick is proud.
